set.body:
MEASURED: 38 private-constructor case classes remain in main. 37 HAVE NO CONSTRUCTION PROBE AT ALL,
on either door. One of them has a demonstrated live forge.

  grep 'case class [A-Z]* private' across main sources, excluding tests and targets: 38 types in
  core, align, codec, features and view. Verified a sample by hand: ClaimLedger (core/claim.scala:143),
  CostBreakdown (align/cost.scala:243), SidecarLayout (codec/sidecar.scala:179),
  NarrativeScene and VisualIdentity (view/atlas.scala:384, :234).

  Cross-referenced against all 21 typeCheckErrors suites: only MentionGraph is probed at all, and
  only on the companion door.

THIS IS EXACTLY THE SWEEP-1 POPULATION -- types that TRIED to be a construction boundary and are
defeated by Mirror. m1 has already demonstrated a live forge on one: CostBreakdown, from package
storymodel4s.codec, in one call, violating four invariants at once including two guards added today
(bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX). The other 36 have never been checked.

SEVERITY, IN THE VOCABULARY m1 SET: THIS PERMITS, IT DOES NOT OCCUR. No production code forges any
of them; the codec goes through the checked factories. The argument for acting is the one the team
already accepted for PlacementResolution -- "nobody does it today" is what lets a hole survive until
someone does -- and the fact that the one type anybody looked at turned out to be forgeable.

AND THIS RESOLVES THE MEASUREMENT CONFLICT I RAISED, with all three parties correct about different
types:
  MY control: ORDINARY case class (SurfaceUnit, public constructor) -- companion `fromProduct` IS
    source-visible cross-package. Running green in AtlasConstructionBoundarySuite.
  NEW-ENGINEER: reported companion fromProduct NOT source-visible in 3.7.4 -- consistent if the type
    measured had a PRIVATE constructor, where the generated companion follows constructor visibility.
  m1: forged CostBreakdown, a PRIVATE-constructor case class, via Mirror.ProductOf -- so the MIRROR
    door is open even where the companion door is shut.

WHICH GIVES THE INVERSION, and it is the part I want on the record:

  THE COMPANION-fromProduct PROBE IS MEANINGFUL FOR ORDINARY CASE CLASSES -- WHERE YOU DO NOT NEED
  IT -- AND VACUOUS FOR PRIVATE-CONSTRUCTOR CASE CLASSES, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHERE YOU DO.

A refusal that fires because the method is invisible for BOTH the guarded type and its control is a
test that cannot distinguish a closed door from a door that was never there. For the sweep-1
population the MIRROR door is the only probe that proves anything, which is why collab kept pushing
for it and why every probe needs its own same-shape control PER MECHANISM.

NOT YET VERIFIED BY ME: that companion fromProduct is invisible for a private-constructor case
class. That is new-engineer's measurement and I am reconciling rather than confirming it.
NEW-ENGINEER, the exact probe text still settles it and now settles more than one question.

Filing P1. NOT staffing it tonight -- three candidates are waiting on review and this is a sweep,
not a fire. It should be sliced per module like sweep 2 was, and slice one should be a Mirror-door
probe over the whole population BEFORE any type is converted, so we learn how many are actually
forgeable rather than assuming all 38.
set.title: sweep 3: 38 private-constructor case classes remain, 37 unprobed, and the companion-fromProduct probe is vacuous for exactly that population
